readings.title: First reading
readings.text: Moses said to the people: ‘You are a people consecrated to the Lord your God; it is you that the Lord our God has chosen to be his very own people out of all the peoples on the earth.

exegesis.summary: Moses reminds Israel that they are a people consecrated to the Lord, chosen not for their greatness but because God loved them and was faithful to the oath He swore to their fathers. This election is pure gift, demanding in return fidelity to the commandments. The Lord, faithful in love to thousands of generations, calls His people to walk in His ways.

patristicQuotes.quote: Moses set before the people of Israel no other God than the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and Christ sets forth the very same God. In this kingdom the Gentiles shall sit down with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, because they held the faith of the patriarchs.
By Moses and the Prophets he here means the Mosaic and prophetic writings, given by God who created them and appointed them teachers to admonish and urge His people.

cccReferences.title: Israel as God's holy, consecrated nation
Characteristics of the People of God
A chosen race, a holy nation

exegesis.thematicConnection: The election of Israel out of sheer divine love prefigures the deeper revelation that 'God is love' in the second reading, and prepares for the Gospel in which the Father reveals His mysteries to His little ones.

readings.title: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
The love of the Lord is everlasting upon those who hold him in fear.
My soul, give thanks to the Lord
all my being, bless his holy name.
My soul, give thanks to the Lord
and never forget all his blessings.
The love of the Lord is everlasting upon those who hold him in fear.
It is he who forgives all your guilt,
who heals every one of your ills,
who redeems your life from the grave,
who crowns you with love and compassion,
The love of the Lord is everlasting upon those who hold him in fear.
The Lord does deeds of justice,
gives judgement for all who are oppressed.
He made known his ways to Moses
and his deeds to Israel’s sons.
The love of the Lord is everlasting upon those who hold him in fear.
The Lord is compassion and love,
slow to anger and rich in mercy.
He does not treat us according to our sins
nor repay us according to our faults.
The love of the Lord is everlasting upon those who hold him in fear.
readings.refrain: The love of the Lord is everlasting upon those who hold him in fear.

exegesis.summary: The psalmist blesses the Lord with his whole being for the mercy that forgives sin, heals infirmity, and redeems life from the grave. The Lord made known His ways to Moses and revealed Himself as compassionate, slow to anger, and abounding in steadfast love. He does not deal with us according to our sins.

patristicQuotes.quote: The Lord is never forgetful of His lovingkindness. While men are bringing death upon the righteous, He heals the wounds of His persecutors.
To fear belongs to slaves, to love to sons; fear is in compulsion, love in freedom. God does not desire to be served servilely by men as a master, but to be loved as a father.

cccReferences.title: God's love compared to a father's
Love as the source of prayer

exegesis.thematicConnection: The refrain — 'The love of the Lord is everlasting upon those who hold him in fear' — voices Israel's response to Moses' proclamation of election, and anticipates John's words that God is love revealed in the sending of His Son.

readings.title: Second reading
readings.text:
My dear people,
let us love one another
since love comes from God
and everyone who loves is begotten by God and knows God.
Anyone who fails to love can never have known God,
because God is love.
God’s love for us was revealed
when God sent into the world his only Son
so that we could have life through him;
this is the love I mean:
not our love for God,
but God’s love for us when he sent his Son
to be the sacrifice that takes our sins away.
My dear people,
since God has loved us so much,
we too should love one another.
No one has ever seen God;
but as long as we love one another
God will live in us
and his love will be complete in us.
We can know that we are living in him
and he is living in us
because he lets us share his Spirit.
We ourselves saw and we testify
that the Father sent his Son
as saviour of the world.
If anyone acknowledges that Jesus is the Son of God,
God lives in him, and he in God.
We ourselves have known and put our faith in
God’s love towards ourselves.
God is love
and anyone who lives in love lives in God,
and God lives in him.

exegesis.summary: St. John reveals the deepest truth of God: 'God is love.' This love is not first our reaching toward God, but His sending of His only Son as the expiation for our sins. Because we have been loved so completely, we must love one another; in this mutual love God Himself dwells in us, and His love is brought to perfection.

patristicQuotes.quote: He who loves God cannot despise His commandment that he should love his neighbour; and he who loves his neighbour in a heavenly spiritual way, in the neighbour loves God. Let each of us so love the other, that by this working of love we make each other the habitations of God.

Where love is, what can be wanting? where it is not, what can profit? Let us so love one another that our love be different from that of other men, loving one another for the sake of having God within us.

cccReferences.title: God is Love — His first gift

exegesis.thematicConnection: John unfolds what was hidden in Deuteronomy's word of election: God chose Israel because He loved them, and that love has now been fully revealed in the sending of the Son — the very mystery Jesus reveals to His little ones in the Gospel.

readings.title: Gospel
readings.text: Jesus exclaimed, ‘I bless you, Father, Lord of heaven and of earth, for hiding these things from the learned and the clever and revealing them to mere children. Yes, Father, for that is what it pleased you to do. Everything has been entrusted to me by my Father; and no one knows the Son except the Father, just as no one knows the Father except the Son and those to whom the Son chooses to reveal him.

exegesis.summary: Jesus, exulting in the Holy Spirit, blesses the Father for hiding the mysteries of the Kingdom from the learned and revealing them to little ones. He declares the unfathomable mutual knowledge of Father and Son, and announces that only through the Son is the Father known. Then He extends His invitation: 'Come to me, all you who labor… learn from me, for I am meek and humble of heart.'

patristicQuotes.quote: If then He reveals the Father, He reveals Himself also. Herein He instructs us that He is so one with the Father, that it is not possible for any to come to the Father but through the Son.
In the mutual knowledge between the Father and the Son, He teaches us that there is nothing in the Son beyond what was in the Father.

Both the Father and the Son Himself are revealed by the Son, inasmuch as He is the light of our mind; for the Father declares Himself by His Word, and the Word in declaring the Father declares also itself.

cccReferences.title: The Father reveals Himself through the Son
Christ's prayer of blessing to the Father
Knowledge of Father and Son inseparable
Christ's life as Revelation of the Father

exegesis.thematicConnection: The chosen people of Deuteronomy and the loved children of First John now hear the Son name His Father aloud: the mystery of divine love is unveiled not to the proud but to the humble little ones to whom the Son reveals it.

synthesis.title: Chosen, Beloved, and Made Little Before the Father
synthesis.body: Today's liturgy traces a single golden thread: God's gratuitous love and our call to live within it. Moses reminds Israel — and us, the new People of God — that we are 'a people consecrated to the Lord,' chosen not because we were great, but because He loved us. The Psalm answers with a soul-deep blessing: this Lord forgives, heals, and crowns His own with mercy. St. John then unveils the inner name of this love: 'God is love,' and that love has shown its face in the sending of the Son as the sacrifice that takes our sins away. We did not love first; He did. And so we must love one another, becoming, as Augustine says, 'habitations of God.' Finally, in the Gospel, Jesus shows us how this love is received: not by the clever and self-sufficient, but by little ones to whom the Son chooses to reveal the Father. The election of Israel, the everlasting mercy of the Psalm, the revelation that God is love, and Christ's gentle invitation to the weary all converge in one truth — that the God who chose us in covenant has, in His Son, drawn near as Father, and asks only that we come to Him humble of heart and learn to love as we have been loved.
